subject: Gen7 core V1 readiness ledger can retire outgoing host on unsequenced/stale FIRST_USEFUL
body: Against current main 633c75be26001d5a4ef6e04c7696e8246713be44 and Primary artifact DUO_OPEN_GEN7_CORE_DEV_ROUND_V1.zip (sha256 1eb02d62d58d8baf42c020993455c96028b5793c34136e2f4fcab63ee4b9e20e), deterministic source-level Kotlin reproduction found a readiness-fencing defect in Fold7PresentationReceiptLedgerGen7 + Fold7HostMigrationLeaseGen7. Current ledger accepts FIRST_USEFUL as the first receipt (no FIRST_PRESENTED predecessor), after which migration.decision() returns RETIRE_OUTGOING_READY. It also accepts a later receipt after Fold7AttemptOwnerGen7.advanceGeneration() because HostIdentity carries only immutable attempt identity/startGeneration, and remains ready after owner.terminal() because the ledger/migration lease do not consult current owner terminal/generation state. Additional deterministic checks show FIRST_INTERACTIVE can skip predecessors, timeNs can regress while frameSequence increases, and duplicate FIRST_* receipts overwrite the original first timestamp/frame. Current V1 adversarial checks: 6/6 targeted invariants FAIL; migration reproduction: useful_without_presented_accepted=true, migration_after_skipped_stage=RETIRE_OUTGOING_READY, post_generation_receipt_accepted=true, ledger_still_ready_after_terminal=true, migration_after_terminal=RETIRE_OUTGOING_READY. This does not prove a production runtime exploit because Gen7 V1 is not wired into production, but it is a MODEL/SOURCE blocker to treating the current core primitive as an exact-current readiness gate. Research is building a hardened pure model and final artifact; production Git write NO.
